rich_narrative.summary:
IRUSA Waqf functions as a permanent endowment pool designed to support the long-term sustainability and emergency humanitarian efforts of Islamic Relief USA <cite id="3">Form 990 (2023)</cite>. Operating out of the United States, the organization was <cite id="1">founded in 1993</cite> to create lasting funding streams for international development and disaster response <cite id="4">Charity Website</cite>. In FY2024, the organization recorded <cite id="3">total revenue of $2,405,280</cite>, marking a 3-year revenue CAGR of <cite id="1">25.7%</cite>. The endowment model focuses on building capital assets to maintain ongoing programs across regions including Pakistan, Gaza, Lebanon, and Yemen <cite id="4">Charity Website</cite>.

While the charity demonstrates structural longevity and maintains a verified theory of change <cite id="1">Charity Navigator</cite>, its overall efficiency and governance metrics reflect notable tradeoffs. Financial reporting shows an unknown program expense ratio due to incomplete expense breakdown data, leaving program efficiency unverified <cite id="1">Charity Navigator</cite>. Additionally, the organization requires <cite id="1">$0.84 in fundraising expenses to raise $1</cite> in contributions, which is significantly less efficient than peer benchmarks <cite id="1">Charity Navigator</cite>. At the same time, the foundation maintains an unusually high reserve level with <cite id="1">392.9 months of operating working capital</cite>, reflecting an endowment-first model rather than immediate field deployment <cite id="1">Charity Navigator</cite>. Donors can support its long-term mission through <cite id="4">sadaqah contributions</cite>.
